extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, computational narratologists, and practitioners building/evaluating LLM-based story generation and understanding systems
extracted.subtask_description: Surveying and guiding the design/evaluation of LLM methods for automatic story generation and understanding with explicit grounding in narrative theory and narratology distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single generalised 'narrative quality' benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the pursuit of a single, generalised benchmark for 'narrative quality', the paper argues progress is better served by more focused efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors warn against attempting a unified definition/benchmark of narrative-related tasks because that makes model comparison difficult. They recommend researchers avoid one-size-fits-all quality metrics and instead adopt more granular, theory-aligned evaluation approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and improve theory-based metrics for individual narrative attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and improve theory-based metrics for individual narrative attributes to incrementally improve model performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create metrics grounded in narratology (i.e., attribute-specific measures) rather than holistic or vague 'story quality' scores. Emphasise incremental, attribute-level evaluation so models can be compared and improved on concrete narrative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct large-scale, theory-driven literary/social/cultural analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct large-scale, theory-driven literary/social/cultural analysis using LLMs and generated/annotated corpora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LLM outputs and dataset-scale processing to perform empirical analyses that connect computational results to literary and cultural theory. This encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and positions model outputs as data for humanities/social-science inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments where model outputs validate or refine narrative theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Create experiments where outputs can be used to validate or refine narrative theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure evaluations and generation experiments so that model behavior provides evidence relevant to narratological hypotheses; use outcomes to iteratively test and potentially update theoretical claims about narrative phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map datasets and tasks to narratological distinctions (taxonomy alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a taxonomy for ongoing efforts that reflect established distinctions in narratology and discover patterns in narrative datasets and tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting or curating datasets and tasks, explicitly map them to narratology concepts (e.g., focalization, plot causality, temporality). This alignment supports clearer task definitions and more meaningful comparisons across models and studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate NLP pipelines and methodological choices (prompting, fine-tuning) in relation to narrative concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine NLP pipeline and methodological trends in prompting and fine-tuning with respect to how they connect to abstract narrative concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess not just raw performance but how methodological choices (prompt engineering, fine-tuning regimes, annotation strategies) enable or obstruct modeling of specific narrative attributes; document these connections to facilitate interdisciplinary understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interdisciplinary collaboration to connect pipelines with abstract narrative concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration enabled by LLMs to connect NLP pipelines with abstract narrative concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve scholars from narrative studies when defining metrics, taxonomies, and evaluation tasks so that computational work reflects domain-theoretic nuance; this improves construct validity of experiments and metrics.
